dedupe_keys.name: esa sentinel 1d mission control simulation of a carrington class solar storm esoc 2025

description: This case study describes a mission-control simulation in which ESA teams rehearsed the launch of Sentinel-1D under a Carrington-class solar storm. The European Space Operations Centre in Darmstadt ran the exercise from mid-September 2025 before the 4 November 2025 launch, with the Space Weather Office activating the Space Safety Centre and the Space Debris Office and other mission managers joining. The scenario had three phases: an X45-class flare that knocked out navigation and tracking, a particle storm causing bit flips, and a coronal mass ejection with a geomagnetic storm that raised drag by up to 400 percent, collapsed grids on the ground and degraded conjunction data. Coverage is one mission plus cross-mission effects. Format and access: a free ESA web story with video; no data or report is released. Licence: ESA website terms, not read. Caveats: it is a narrative account without measured results. It supports resilience and emergency response planning for space operations and shows why space weather and collision-risk services must be coordinated. Related catalogue records are the 2024 solar maximum operator review and the ESA collision avoidance challenge dataset.

name: ESA Sentinel-1D mission control simulation of a Carrington-class solar storm (ESOC, 2025)
outcomes: Teams handled loss of navigation, single-event upsets and multiple collision warnings, and learned that satellite drag could rise 400 percent and degrade conjunction data, making avoidance decisions uncertain; the results feed European space weather service design. No quantitative performance figures are reported.
